questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 and 24 minutes respectively. After both are opened together for 6 minutes, the rate of pipe A becomes half, and pipe B becomes double its original. In how many more minutes will the tank be full?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 and 24 minutes respectively. After both are opened together for 6 minutes, the rate of pipe A becomes half, and pipe B becomes double its original. In how many more minutes will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
Combined rate of A & B = 1/18 + 1/24 = 7/72 per minute.

Work done in first 6 minutes = 6 × 7/72 = 7/12. Remaining = 5/12.

New rates: A = 1/36, B = 1/12. Combined = 1/36 + 3/36 = 4/36 = 1/9 per minute.

Time required = (5/12) ÷ (1/9) = 45/12 = 3.75 minutes = 3 min 45 sec.

questions.question: If A, B, and C are three amounts of money such that B is the simple interest on A, and C is the simple interest on B, all for the same time and at the same rate of interest, then which of the following is true?
questions.questionHtml: If A, B, and C are three amounts of money such that B is the simple interest on A, and C is the simple interest on B, all for the same time and at the same rate of interest, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Let r = (rate × time)/100.

Then B = A·r and C = B·r.

So, B² = (A·r)² = A·(A·r²) = A·(B·r) = A·C.

Hence B² = AC.

questions.solution:
tan 45° = height / shadow.

1 = 20 / shadow.

Hence shadow = 20 m.

questions.question: A hemisphere of radius 5 cm is carved from a sphere. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
questions.questionHtml: A hemisphere of radius 5 cm is carved from a sphere. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
questions.solution:
Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) π r³.

= (2/3) π (5)³ = (2/3) π × 125 = 250π/3 cm³.

questions.question: A solid sphere is placed inside a cube such that it touches all six faces. What percentage of the cube's volume is NOT occupied by the sphere?
questions.questionHtml: A solid sphere is placed inside a cube such that it touches all six faces. What percentage of the cube's volume is NOT occupied by the sphere?
questions.solution:
Let cube side = 2r.

Cube volume = 8r³;

sphere volume = (4/3)π r³.

Sphere fraction = (4π/3)/8 = π/6 ≈ 0.5236 ≈ 52.36%.

Not occupied = 100 − 52.36 ≈ 47.64% ≈ 47.67%.

questions.question: The sides of a rectangular prism are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. If the volume of the prism is 960 cm³, what is the length of its longest side?
questions.questionHtml: The sides of a rectangular prism are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. If the volume of the prism is 960 cm³, what is the length of its longest side?
questions.solution:
Sides = 4x, 5x, 6x. Volume = 4x · 5x · 6x = 120x³.

120x³ = 960 → x³ = 8 → x = 2.

Longest side = 6x = 12 cm.

questions.question: A conical bucket is cut at one-third its height from the top. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two parts (top part to bottom part)?
questions.questionHtml: A conical bucket is cut at one-third its height from the top. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two parts (top part to bottom part)?
questions.solution:
Top is a smaller similar cone of height h/3 of the full cone.

Volume ratio (small : full) = (1/3)³ = 1 : 27.

Hence top : bottom = 1 : (27 − 1) = 1 : 26.

questions.question: If tan A + cot A = 2 and A ∈ (0, π/2), then what is sin A + cos A?
questions.questionHtml: If tan A + cot A = 2 and A ∈ (0, π/2), then what is sin A + cos A?
questions.solution:
Let t = tan A. t + 1/t = 2 → (t − 1)² = 0 → t = 1.

So A = π/4, and sin A = cos A = 1/√2.

sin A + cos A = 2 · (1/√2) = √2.

questions.question: What is the value of sin 20° cos 10° + cos 20° sin 10°?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of sin 20° cos 10° + cos 20° sin 10°?
questions.solution:
Use sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B.

sin 20° cos 10° + cos 20° sin 10° = sin(20° + 10°) = sin 30°.

= 1/2.

questions.question: The graph of y = 4x − 5 passes through which point?
questions.questionHtml: The graph of y = 4x − 5 passes through which point?
questions.solution:
Check (1, -1): 4(1) − 5 = -1 ✓.

Check (0, -5): 4(0) − 5 = -5 ✓.

Check (2, 3): 4(2) − 5 = 3 ✓.

All three points satisfy the equation, so the answer is All the above.

questions.question: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 60° and a radius of 9 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of π/3 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 60° and a radius of 9 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of π/3 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.solution:
π/3 radians = 180°/3 = 60°.

Both sectors have the same angle (60°) and same radius (9 cm).

Hence the ratio of their areas is 1 : 1.

questions.question: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which:
questions.questionHtml: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which:

options.text: Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
options.html: Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.

options.text: Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.
options.html: Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

questions.solution:
By definition, in a parallelogram both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal in length.

Right-angle and perpendicular-diagonal conditions apply to special cases (rectangle, rhombus).

Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one leg of 5 cm. A second right-angled triangle is similar to the first, and its hypotenuse is 39 cm. What is the area of the second triangle?
questions.questionHtml: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one leg of 5 cm. A second right-angled triangle is similar to the first, and its hypotenuse is 39 cm. What is the area of the second triangle?
questions.solution:
Other leg of first triangle = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12.

Area of first triangle = (1/2) × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

Similarity ratio = 39/13 = 3, so area ratio = 3² = 9.

Area of second triangle = 30 × 9 = 270 cm².

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, a line segment BD is a diagonal such that AB = CD and ∠ABD = ∠CDB. Are the triangles ABD and CDB congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.questionHtml: In a quadrilateral ABCD, a line segment BD is a diagonal such that AB = CD and ∠ABD = ∠CDB. Are the triangles ABD and CDB congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.solution:
In △ABD and △CDB: AB = CD (given).

∠ABD = ∠CDB (given).

BD = DB (common side).

Hence by SAS rule, △ABD ≅ △CDB.

questions.question: If sin x = 3/5 and x ∈ (0, π/2), then find (1 + tan x) / (1 − tan x).
questions.questionHtml: If sin x = 3/5 and x ∈ (0, π/2), then find (1 + tan x) / (1 − tan x).
questions.solution:
sin x = 3/5, cos x = 4/5 (since x is in first quadrant).

tan x = 3/4.

(1 + tan x)/(1 − tan x) = (1 + 3/4)/(1 − 3/4) = (7/4)/(1/4) = 7.

questions.question: The length of each of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 10 cm. What is the approximate distance from the external point to the center of the circle, if the radius is 6 cm?
questions.questionHtml: The length of each of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 10 cm. What is the approximate distance from the external point to the center of the circle, if the radius is 6 cm?
questions.solution:
Tangent ⟂ radius, so distance² = tangent² + radius².

= 10² + 6² = 100 + 36 = 136.

Distance = √136 ≈ 11.66 ≈ 12 cm.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with legs of length 5 and 12. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with legs of length 5 and 12. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution:
Hypotenuse = √(5² + 12²) = 13.

For a right triangle: r = (a + b − c)/2 where c is hypotenuse.

r = (5 + 12 − 13)/2 = 4/2 = 2.

questions.question: What is the result of (0.5³ + 0.1³ − 0.6³) ÷ (3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × 0.6)?
questions.solution:
Note 0.5 + 0.1 = 0.6. So with a = 0.5, b = 0.1, c = 0.6 we have a + b = c.

Identity: a³ + b³ − c³ = −3abc when a + b = c.

So, numerator = −3(0.5)(0.1)(0.6); denominator = 3(0.5)(0.1)(0.6).

Ratio = −1.
